To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of archetypes as elements of a Dual Model architecture is a promising approach for integrating heterogeneous data sources in a semantic way, with a clear separation of information and knowledge.
Archetypes can be used to integrate clinical information from heterogeneous sources, adding at the sametime a semantic meaning.
the Dual Model approach, based on Reference Model and Archetypes, is a suitable approach to integrate and standardize heterogeneous clinical data sources.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of a Dual-Model approach to integrate heterogeneous clinical data sources.
the use of archetypes as a way of adding semantics to clinical data and the development of LinkEHR-ED, a tool for creating archetypes for semantic integration of clinical data.
the development of an archetype-based architecture for semantic integration of clinical data sources, and a tool to support the development of archetypes for this integration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
archetypes are an excellent way to represent the semantics of clinical data and to integrate and standardize them, as well as to maintain the information of the EHR.

the Dual Model architecture and its archetype representation can provide an effective way to integrate heterogeneous clinical data, and LinkEHR-ED is an useful and friendly tool to create archetypes in a simple and easy way for the integration purposes.

the proposed approach for the integration of heterogeneous clinical data using archetypes as elements of integration, is a good alternative for the integration of data coming from different sources, with a high degree of flexibility and reusability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how archetypes can be used as a semantic bridge for integrating clinical data from heterogeneous sources.

the use of the Dual Model approach for integration purposes allows to maintain the clinical meaning of the integrated data, which is very important when the integration is performed in order to be used for clinical purposes.
the proposed tool is able to generate archetypes for clinical semantic integration from a set of clinical data sources, using a set of templates for the definition of archetypes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of archetypes in clinical data integration processes is feasible and that the development of archetypes for this kind of tasks is a collaborative and interdisciplinary work.
archetypes are an appropriate tool for semantic integration and normalization of heterogeneous clinical data.
archetypes are a very useful tool for semantic integration of clinical data sources and can be used to standardize the data of heterogeneous systems.
